name: Gemariah
title: The Scribe, Son of Shaphan
summary: Gemariah was the son of the scribe Shaphan and one of the prominent officials in Judah during King Jehoiakim's reign. He is known for his role concerning the prophet Jeremiah's prophecies, when he allowed Baruch to read aloud Jeremiah's scroll in his chamber at the temple. Gemariah was among those who warned King Jehoiakim against burning the scroll containing the Lord's words.

keyEvents.title: Baruch reads the scroll in Gemariah's chamber
keyEvents.description: Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, read aloud the prophet's words to all the people from Gemariah's chamber in the house of the Lord, at the upper court near the entrance of the new gate.

keyEvents.title: Micaiah hears the words and reports to the officials
keyEvents.description: Micaiah son of Gemariah heard all the words of the Lord from the scroll and went down to the scribe's chamber to tell the officials what he had heard.

keyEvents.title: The officials send for Baruch
keyEvents.description: After Micaiah reported the contents of the scroll, the officials, including Gemariah, sent for Baruch to hear the words directly.

keyEvents.title: Gemariah warns the king not to burn the scroll
keyEvents.description: When King Jehoiakim began cutting up and burning the scroll containing Jeremiah's prophecies, Gemariah was among those who urgently pleaded with the king not to burn it, but the king would not listen to them.

keyEvents.title: The role of Gemariah's father Shaphan as background
keyEvents.description: Gemariah's father Shaphan was the scribe who played a key role during King Josiah's religious reform when the Book of the Law was found in the temple, giving the family a prominent position.
